comments.text: I have for decades been proud of Botswana. They can teach many other African countries a thing or two. Let's not understate the influence the European first lady had in the first president's decision to follow the path of democracy and transparency. Under British colonial law, mineral resources belonged to the tribe in whose territory they were situated. But the Kharma government decided that the diamond and other mineral wealth would be shared equally amongst all Botswanans. comments.text: Dumela! The Delta is a beautiful place and refreshing to watch Botswana. Something to add, it is nolonger acceptable to say there are 8 main or major tribes. It was something that was even in school books in the 80's & 90's becoz during the protectorate times the British selected 8 Tswana tribes for their administration purposes. In modern Botswana we want a society that belong to all its pple whether Tswana or Non Tswana without hierarchies, thats why it was stopped. And what is interesting of the 8 tribes selected by the British non is senior according to Tswana culture. In Setswana culture Bahurutshi are the more senior who are not part of the former 8 main tribes.

replies.author: @bosezwitolo8382
replies.text: The San are the first pple to settle in the area that is now called Botswana, but the Tswana speaking pple are not the first Bantu to settle in area. The first Bantu pple to settle in the area are those found in the northern part of the country who are still there. The evidence is the archaeological remains of stones ruins similar to bo Zimbabwe and Khami Ruins which is usually found were ever they settled. Other Bantu (Mbukushu and Bayei) pple are those in north west of the country who again non-Tswana the really custodian with San of the wildlife. Again all this corrections not done through civil strife but through mafoko a kgotla amantle, mmua lebe. We have heard in some African countries pple kill each other becoz they belong to a different tribes. Hope again we learn from wild dogs.
